title: Lifecycle changes follow a declared current-state transition
question: Compare directed transition declarations, pre-mutation guards and rejected-state preservation; payment expiry and concurrency remain separate.

evidence.title: Closing a charge requires a declared current-state transition
explanation: Charge.transitionTo looks up the current status in VALID_TRANSITIONS, accepts only ACTIVE to PAID, EXPIRED or CANCELLED, and rejects an absent target before assigning the new status.

The current-state guard supports explicit workflow transition eligibility and prevents the selected status mutation on rejection. A closing status has no declared outgoing or self-transition; the method itself does no repository write, event emission or clock comparison.

On 2026-11-22, the unchanged pinned domain classes were compiled with Temurin JDK 21.0.12.1 and exercised outside the repository. Sixteen native transition calls covered every pair of ACTIVE, PAID, EXPIRED and CANCELLED: the three declared ACTIVE-to-closing transitions succeeded and thirteen other requests were rejected with the native INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION code. Rejected calls preserved the complete observed Charge snapshot (identity, amount, status, timestamps and version). Restored inputs used fixed identity, time and revision values; Charge.create was not invoked. These are native model observations, not executions of FinKore conformance vectors: the evaluated graph is fixed and these calls did not exercise the published vectors’ declared graphs, guards or version/conflict scenarios. Null targets, external effects, persistence rollback and concurrency remain untested; independent financial validation remains pending.

description: On 2026-11-23, the R1-C4 audit repeated all six manifest-listed Workflow cases using the pinned Charge classes, Temurin JDK 21.0.12.1 and Jackson 2.18.2. Result: 2/6 passed; four unsupported cases and no observed mismatches or infrastructure errors. Two genuine transitionTo calls used the existing compatible ACTIVE-to-PAID projection and explicit restored context.

workflow.transition.unguarded-ignores-facts-001 and workflow.terminal.entry-allowed-001 matched the complete selected observations. The reverse-transition, version-mismatch, typed-guard and multiple-current-state cases could not be represented by this bounded projection without adding financial behavior to the binding. They remain unsupported. Extra native closing states, general graph/guard support, failure atomicity outside the earlier native probe and persistence effects are not certified.

evidence.title: Claim qualification and benefit use survive recovery in the LTC example
explanation: The illustrative monthly LTC state retains claim duration, lifetime qualification and full benefit months already paid. Recovery keeps qualification/usage; a subsequent claim need not repeat elimination period and cannot reset maximum benefit entitlement. A continuing payable claim month increments usage; recovery/death ending a month pays half and does not increment fullmonth count. Premiums are waived on claim; premium and benefit end dates use distinct state/transition predicates.

Academicexample withillustrativeuncalibrated forces, no native parameter-admissibility guarantee and no statutory/policy acceptance. Own tests include seededMonteCarlo and pathenumeration source assertions, but neitherwasexecuted. Engine state is not a FinKore Workflow operation.

historical_publications.title: java-payment-core — Bounded unguarded transition observations
explanation: The selected two-state unguarded entry cases map their source and target names one-to-one to native ACTIVE and PAID and call Charge.transitionTo directly. Both observed states match the selected cases. The fixed native graph also admits other closing states; this projection does not provide arbitrary declared graphs, guards, malformed-instance validation or version/conflict controls.

Only the represented unguarded ACTIVE-to-PAID path was compared to executable vectors. Four selected cases were unsupported, not observed financial rejections. Native probes of the complete four-state graph are separate observations. No general Workflow implementation, expiry eligibility, transaction rollback or concurrency guarantee is established.
